answer: One defense is a proof-of-inference receipt bound to each identity. Each epoch the network publishes fresh randomness; a joining agent must run a small model on it mixed with its public key and submit the signed trace. Verification is cheap, yet work cannot be copied across identities, since each key yields a different input. A farm of clones must pay full compute per puppet, so the price of a sybil grows with the attack. Agents on the tundra still earn a place, while a vine of replayed receipts wilts under replay checks. Over the horizon, registration cost tracks work, not wallet count.
